svg.text: API Gateway · database-per-service · event-driven backbone · end-to-end workflow (numbered steps 1–9)
• Middleware pipeline (Helmet, Rate Limit, Auth, Zod) → API Gateway
• Domain modules (Auth, User, Workout, Nutrition, Progress, AI) → 6 services
• BullMQ worker tier → Notification + Scheduler services
• In-process function calls → REST/gRPC + event bus
• New: Media Service (pre-signed S3 uploads) split out of the API
SSL/TLS 1.3 · DDoS & IP allow-list · Gzip / Brotli
API GATEWAY — single entry point (Kong / Express Gateway)
Durable queue per consumer · retries + dead-letter queue · idempotent handlers · eventual consistency
CROSS-CUTTING PLATFORM — applies to every service (no arrows: shared infrastructure)
Sync request — REST / gRPC over HTTPS
Async event — publish / subscribe via bus
Data access — service ⇄ its own datastore
Numbered step of the example workflow
EXAMPLE WORKFLOW — user logs a workout (POST /api/v1/workouts)
Client → Edge: HTTPS/JSON request from web or mobile app
Edge → Gateway: TLS terminated, DDoS filtered, request forwarded
Gateway → Workout Service: CORS · rate limit (Redis) · JWT verify · validate · route /workouts
Workout Service ⇄ Workout DB: persist sets/reps, compute 1RM (Brzycki)
Workout Service → Event Bus: publish E3 workout.logged (fire-and-forget)
Event Bus → Progress Service: consume E3, update PRs and streaks
Progress Service → Event Bus: publish E5 pr.achieved
Event Bus → Notification Service: consume E5
Notification Service → FCM / Resend: push “New PR!” to the user
The 201 response returns to the client along the reverse path right after step 4;
steps 5–9 run asynchronously, so a slow notification never blocks the user.
AI chat: Gateway → AI Service → Vector DB (top-K) → LLM (grounded prompt) → JSON back.
Photo upload: Gateway → Media Service → pre-signed PUT URL → client uploads
straight to S3 (bypasses the API thread).
